subject: physics
intro: Physics leads to work that models and engineers the physical world — fundamental research, nuclear technology, machine and system design, and the lecture halls that train the next generation.

roles.title: Physicists
roles.what: Conduct research into physical phenomena, develop theories from observation and experiment, and devise methods to apply physical laws and theories — from quantum field theory to the physics of materials and energy.
roles.where: The Supplement-fed lessons carry you there: quantum foundations and field theory, statistical mechanics, special and general relativity, and the electrodynamics-maxwell and solid-state-physics expert units.

roles.title: Nuclear Engineers
roles.what: Research and solve problems in the release, control and use of nuclear energy — reactor design and operation, radiation protection and nuclear waste disposal — applying nuclear science theory to practical systems.
roles.where: Unit 5, Nuclear physics — the nuclear model of the atom, radioactive decay, half-life calculations and safety precautions — is the syllabus's direct line into reactor and waste-disposal engineering.

roles.title: Natural Sciences Managers
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate research and development in the physical sciences, mathematics and engineering — leading laboratory teams, setting priorities and deciding which experiments and projects get funded.
roles.where: Physical quantities and measurement techniques (topic 1.1) plus the experimental discipline threaded through every unit build the lab judgment such managers direct; energy resources (1.7) shows the applied side.

roles.title: Mechanical Engineers
roles.what: Design tools, engines, machines and other mechanically functioning equipment, and oversee their installation, operation, maintenance and repair — from heat, gas and power systems to vehicles and manufacturing plant.
roles.where: Motion, forces and energy (unit 1) — Newton's laws, momentum and collisions, energy, work and power, pressure — is the mechanical engineer's toolkit, extended by the projectile-motion and fluid-dynamics lessons.

roles.title: Physics Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach university courses on the laws of matter and energy — mechanics, thermal physics, electromagnetism, quantum theory — often combining teaching with research at the frontiers of the discipline.
roles.where: The six-unit arc — motion and energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, nuclear physics, space physics — is the standard undergraduate lecture sequence you would go on to teach.
